description:
Worldsmith Console Commands
Reshape the Sector from the console.
v1.3.0 for Starsector 0.98a-RC8

Download: latest release (GitHub)
Requires: Console Commands, LazyLib, Nexerelin
Can be added to a running save, but not removed from one.
Java: runs on Java 27 (tested with Mikohime) and on the game's standard Java 17.
AI use disclaimer: Most of the code was written by AI (Claude Opus 5.5).

What you can do

Build worlds: planets, moons, rings, asteroid and debris fields, companion stars, or whole new star systems, black holes and neutron stars included.
Bend orbits: push a planet farther out or speed it up, in percent, reverse it, or tidally lock a moon behind its planet.
Terraform and tweak: change a planet's type, size or color, and rename planets, systems and whole factions.
Found factions: a new Nexerelin faction with its own name, flag, lore, ships and personality.
Steer the 4X: set each faction's share of colony expeditions in percent, strengthen or weaken factions, send armadas, start rebellions.
End it all: total war, total peace, or the apocalypse: Remnant raids, orbital bombardment or revolution.

Update 1.3.0

exportsystem: saves a star system to a JSON file with everything it's made of, so modders can build it into their own mod.
importsystem: rebuilds a saved system in hyperspace, in any save, so you can share your systems with others. Alone, it lists your exports.
addwreck: a derelict ship to salvage or recover, by size, faction or exact ship (e.g. addwreck paragon).
warfocus: a faction aims all its Nexerelin invasions and raids at one enemy (e.g. warfocus hegemony tritachyon).

All commands
Here are all commands and their options. You can also read them in the README on GitHub, or in the game: open the console with Ctrl+Backspace and type help worldsmith or wshelp.

How to read this list: options in [brackets] are optional, and a|b means "a or b". Type
names as shown on the map: case doesn't matter, underscores count as spaces, and IDs
work too. Without a name, most commands use the planet whose dialog is open.

LOOKING THINGS UP
=================

showsystem [system]
Every planet, moon and station of a system, with type, hazard, owner and resources.

planetinfo [planet]
Everything about one planet: size, orbit, industries, its conditions and how much each
adds to the hazard.

planettypes [filter]  /  startypes [filter]
All planet or star types, modded ones included. The filter shows only types whose name
contains it.

visit <planet|station|star>
Opens its dialog from anywhere.

findplanet <filters>
Searches the sector and lists the nearest 20 matches. Combine any of:
- a condition such as farmland_rich, or a group such as farmland, ore or ruins (wshelp
conditions lists them all)
- -toxic_atmosphere: must not have it
- habitable, uncolonized, colonized
- type:jungle: that planet type
- hazard<150: hazard below 150% (also <=, >, >=)
- within:20: at most 20 light-years from you
- owner:hegemony: colonies of that faction
- all: also planets you haven't surveyed
Example: findplanet habitable farmland hazard<150 within:20

PLANETS AND COLONIES
====================

terraform [planet] <type> [keep]
Changes an uncolonized planet's type and rolls new conditions that fit it (planettypes
lists the types).
- keep: only the type changes and the conditions stay; this also works on colonies

rename <current name> <new name>
Renames a planet, station or colony.
- put a > between the names if you're unsure where the current one ends
- with a planet's dialog open, just rename <new name>
- rename system <system> <new name>: the system, its star and the planets named after
it (Glith I becomes Hakeball I). Stars always follow their system's name.
- rename faction <faction> <new name>: a faction, everywhere; reset as the new name
undoes it

recolor [planet] <color>
Tints a planet, moon or star. Only the look changes.
- red, orange, yellow, gold, green, teal, cyan, blue, purple, pink, white, grey,
brown, black
- a hex color such as #3080ff
- random
- reset: the standard look of its type

addplanet [type|random] [name]
A planet at your distance from the star, generated like vanilla's.

addmoon <planet> [type|random] [name]
A moon at your distance from the planet, or in its first free orbit.

moveplanet <planet>
Moves it, with its moons, to your distance and angle.

resizeplanet [planet] <percent|auto>
Makes it wider or narrower.
- a percentage: 150% makes it 1.5 times as wide, 200% twice as wide, 50% half as wide
- auto: a normal size for its type

orbit [planet] [options]
Changes the orbit of a planet, moon or companion star. Without options it shows which
way it circles and how many days one orbit takes. Options can be combined:
- distance 150%: 1.5 times as far out (50% = half as far). It keeps its speed, so a
wider orbit takes longer.
- speed 200%: twice as fast (50% = half as fast)
- reverse: circles the other way
- tidallock: for moons. The moon always stays behind its planet, away from the star,
in the planet's shadow, where a neutron star's pulsar beam can't reach it. speed or
reverse ends the lock.
Moons, stations and rings move with it. Example: orbit Corvus_V distance 150%, then
orbit Corvus_VA tidallock.

popcap [colony] <size|off>
The colony stops growing at that size. It never shrinks a colony.
- off: removes the cap

treatasnpccolony [colony] [off]
Nexerelin treats it like its own expedition colonies: the AI builds it up as it grows,
and Nexerelin's size limit for such colonies applies.
- off: removes that mark

SYSTEMS, STARS AND SPACE
========================

newsystem <name> [star type] [full|empty]
In hyperspace, a new star system at your position, with an inner and a fringe jump
point. A popup asks how to fill it, unless you say so in advance:
- full: planets, moons, rings and stable locations, like a random system
- empty: only the star
Without a star type it picks one at random; black holes and neutron stars work too.
The star is called "<name> Prime".

addstar [star type|random] [name]
A second or third star at your position, orbiting the main star: a binary or trinary
system.

addring [planet] <type>
Around the star at your distance from it, or around the named planet.
- belt: an asteroid belt with asteroids
- dust: a dusty ring that looks like debris
- ice: an ice ring
- magfield: a magnetic field

addobject <type>
At your position, orbiting the star.
- stable_location: an empty stable orbit, where a relay, buoy or array can be built
- comm_relay: helps the stability of colonies in the system
- nav_buoy: fleets travel faster in the system
- sensor_array: better sensor range in the system
- comm_relay_makeshift, nav_buoy_makeshift, sensor_array_makeshift: weaker versions
- inactive_gate: a gate
Relays, buoys and arrays start unclaimed, so you claim them like any other.

addfield <asteroids|debris> [small|large]
At your position.
- asteroids: an asteroid field
- debris: a debris field you can salvage
- small / large: its size (otherwise in between)

addwreck [small|medium|large|civilian] [faction|ship]
A derelict ship next to you to salvage or recover, e.g. addwreck paragon.

addjumppoint [name]
A two-way jump point where you are. In a system, it leads out to hyperspace; in
hyperspace, it leads into the nearest system (at most 3 light-years away).

hyperclouds <clear|add> [radius]
In hyperspace, around you.
- clear: removes the clouds and the storms in them
- add: grows new clouds (star systems keep their clear space)
- radius: 0.5 to 5 light-years, 1 if you leave it out

REMOVING THINGS
===============

Everything here asks Yes/Cancel first.

removeplanet <planet>  /  removemoon <moon>
Uninhabited planets and moons, and the second or third star of a system. Rings and
debris around them go with them.

removering [planet] [belt|ring|magfield]
Without a planet, the belt, ring or field around the star nearest to you. With a
planet, all its rings, or only the kind you name.

removeobject [type|name]
The nearest object where you are, the nearest of a type, or one by name.
- stable, relay, buoy, sensor, gate: the objects addobject makes
- field: an asteroid or debris field
- jumppoint: a jump point made with addjumppoint (both ends)

NEW FACTIONS
============

spawnfaction <name> [options]
Founds a new faction. A popup asks for anything you leave out and shows the planets
before anything happens.
- here / random: in your system, or at a random empty place ("Pick another place"
rolls again)
- small / medium / large: 1, 3 or 5 colonies
- red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink: its color on the map. There
are 8 slots, one per color; spawnfaction list shows which are free.
- like <faction>: it uses that faction's ships, weapons and way of fighting. Without
it, a random faction's.
It gets a random player flag and empty lore, and Nexerelin runs it like any other
faction: diplomacy, wars, invasions, alliances. A slot frees up again when its faction
has no colonies left.

factionflag <faction> [option]
Changes any faction's flag.
- no option: a popup shows the flags as pictures; browse with Next/Previous or the
arrow keys
- random: a random player flag
- a number: that player flag (factionflag list numbers them)
- another faction: copies its flag
- reset: its own flag again

factionlore <faction> [option]
The text on the faction's page in the Intel screen. Works for every faction.
- no option: shows the text
- any text: replaces it (a | starts a new paragraph; don't use ;, the console splits
commands there)
- add <text>: adds a paragraph
- reset: brings back the original

factionillegal <faction> [<commodity> illegal|legal | reset]
What a faction bans: its markets sell it only on the black market.
- reset: undoes every change made with this command

factionships <faction> <style>
Which ships its new fleets use.
- lowtech, midline, hightech: only ships of that tech level
- pirate: pirate and low tech ships
- all: every ship the sector's factions use
- like <faction>: copies that faction completely: the same ships, the same weapons and
the same way of fighting. For example, like tritachyon makes it fly Tri-Tachyon
ships with Tri-Tachyon tactics.

factiondoctrine <faction> <preset>
How its fleets are put together and how they fight. Presets add up (for example
aggressive, then carriers, then elite); a new one replaces an earlier one that sets
the same thing.
- aggressive: its captains charge in and fight to the end
- cautious: its captains keep their distance and pull back sooner
- carriers: mostly carriers and fighters
- phase: mostly phase ships
- warships: mostly gun ships, few carriers or phase ships
- elite: fewer ships, but the best quality and officers
- swarm: many cheap, small ships with weak officers
- capitals: mostly big ships
- reset: back to the doctrine of the faction it copies

factionpersonality <faction> <type>
How it behaves towards others.
- warlike: declares war easily and tires of it slowly
- peaceful: never starts wars itself and tires of them quickly
- pirate: Nexerelin treats it as a pirate faction: hostile to everyone except pirates,
free ports, nothing illegal
- lawful: back to normal diplomacy after pirate
- expansionist: sends colony expeditions often
- isolationist: sends no colony expeditions
- normal: undoes all of the above

FACTION STRENGTH
================

factionpower <faction> [clear]
Colonies, stability, unrest, disrupted industries, garrisons, Nexerelin invasion
points and troop reserves, and any Worldsmith effects with how long they last.
- clear: ends the Worldsmith effects early

weakenfaction <faction> [1-3]
First shows what will happen in each colony, then asks. It all wears off by itself.
- 1: unrest for about 6 months
- 2: also a 6-month growth freeze, weaker garrisons, defenses disrupted for 4 months,
fewer invasion points
- 3: lasts up to 3 years: 3-year growth freeze, stability -3 fading by 1 a year,
military and ship industries disrupted for 1-2 years, drained troops and invasion
points

strengthenfaction <faction> [1-3]
The same in reverse.
- 1: clears unrest and disruptions, lifts Worldsmith growth freezes
- 2: also repairs garrisons, adds troops and invasion points, +2 stability for 6
months
- 3: also +3 stability fading by 1 a year, and many more invasion points

expeditions [option]
Nexerelin's colony expeditions. Nexerelin sends one every few months and picks the
faction by share.
- no options: every faction's share and how often expeditions come
- <faction> 30%: that faction sends 30% of all expeditions; the others share the rest
in their usual proportions. 100% = only that faction.
- <faction> off: it sends none
- <faction> reset: its usual share again
- frequency 200%: expeditions come twice as often (50% = half as often)
- reset: everything back to normal

WAR AND PEACE
=============

wars [faction]
Who is at war with whom, the alliances, and how war-weary each faction is. With a
faction: its relation (-100 to 100) with every other faction.

totalwar [withplayer]
Every faction with colonies goes to war with every other one, and all alliances break
up. Asks first.
- withplayer: you join in too (with a commission you share your employer's wars
anyway)

totalpeace [all] [withplayer]
Every faction with colonies makes peace. Asks first.
- all: pirates too
- withplayer: you too

armada <faction> [system] [small|medium|large]
That faction's war fleet jumps into the system (or the one you are in), attacks its
biggest colony for about two months, then leaves. If the two factions aren't at war,
only the armada turns hostile; no war is declared.
- small / medium / large: its size (medium if you leave it out)

warfocus <faction> <enemy> [days]
The faction aims all its invasions and raids at that enemy (default 180 days).

rebellion [colony] [faction]
A Nexerelin rebellion in one colony. The rebels fight for the faction you name, or for
one Nexerelin picks, or for independence. If they win, the colony changes hands.

APOCALYPSE
==========

apocalypse <scenario> [all] asks first. Your own colonies are spared unless you add all.

remnant
An elite Remnant armada attacks every inhabited system for about two months, then
leaves.

bombard
Every colony is saturation-bombed into ruins; story-critical worlds survive. This
can't be undone.

revolution
Nexerelin rebellions break out in every colony of size 3 or more.

SHARING SYSTEMS
===============

exportsystem [system]
Saves a system to a JSON file (saves/common/worldsmith), e.g. for your own mod.

importsystem [file] [new name]
Rebuilds a saved system at your position in hyperspace, without colonies. Alone, it
lists your exports.

Credits: LazyWizard and Lukas04 (Console Commands), LazyWizard (LazyLib), Histidine (Nexerelin). MIT license.

  - <faction> 30%: that faction sends 30% of all expeditions; the others share the rest
    in their usual proportions. 100% = only that faction.
  - <faction> off: it sends none
  - <faction> reset: its usual share again
  - frequency 200%: expeditions come twice as often (50% = half as often)
  - reset: everything back to normal

WAR AND PEACE
=============

wars [faction]
  Who is at war with whom, the alliances, and how war-weary each faction is. With a
  faction: its relation (-100 to 100) with every other faction.

totalwar [withplayer]
  Every faction with colonies goes to war with every other one, and all alliances break
  up. Asks first.
  - withplayer: you join in too (with a commission you share your employer's wars
    anyway)

totalpeace [all] [withplayer]
  Every faction with colonies makes peace. Asks first.
  - all: pirates too
  - withplayer: you too

armada <faction> [system] [small|medium|large]
  That faction's war fleet jumps into the system (or the one you are in), attacks its
  biggest colony for about two months, then leaves. If the two factions aren't at war,
  only the armada turns hostile; no war is declared.
  - small / medium / large: its size (medium if you leave it out)

warfocus <faction> <enemy> [days]
  The faction aims all its invasions and raids at that enemy (default 180 days).

rebellion [colony] [faction]
  A Nexerelin rebellion in one colony. The rebels fight for the faction you name, or for
  one Nexerelin picks, or for independence. If they win, the colony changes hands.

APOCALYPSE
==========

apocalypse <scenario> [all] asks first. Your own colonies are spared unless you add all.

remnant
  An elite Remnant armada attacks every inhabited system for about two months, then
  leaves.

bombard
  Every colony is saturation-bombed into ruins; story-critical worlds survive. This
  can't be undone.

revolution
  Nexerelin rebellions break out in every colony of size 3 or more.

SHARING SYSTEMS
===============

exportsystem [system]
  Saves a system to a JSON file (saves/common/worldsmith), e.g. for your own mod.

importsystem [file] [new name]
  Rebuilds a saved system at your position in hyperspace, without colonies. Alone, it
  lists your exports.
